chapter: Latin bands, Wilbur DeParis and Goodman
title: With Perez Prado in South America; meeting his wife in Argentina
summary: In 1952 he and Paul Webster were featured trumpets with Perez Prado, the band broke up unpaid in Santiago, and he had met his Argentinian wife.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yes. Well, I went with Cab, it was '51. To South America. We came back. '52 I went back down there with Perez Prado. And Paul Webster and myself were the trumpet players the featured trumpet players with Perez Prado's band. We went over the same, played the same carnival in Montevideo that Cab -- that we did with Cab, so after that we played Brazil and a few places with Prado. And then when we left Prado in Argentina. That's where I met my wife.

She's Argentinian. I left Perez Prado, there. We played Santiago, Chile, he also had Michael -- Gene Michael in the band. Saxophone player. Gene Michael was a famous first lead man, with Cecil's band. He was in that band. Gene Michael, Paul Wilson and myself were -- went in that band together. And then we came back to -- because

we weren't getting paid. Perez Prado, he didn't pay us off and he had a lot of money problems with the band and so we broke up and -- inSantiago, Chile. And came back to New York. Now that was the end of Perez Prado as far as we were concerned. Course he continued on with his band and I did a lot of work -- that's when I started work -- doing subs for Wilbur's band. Gigging around at other little places I could get.
